findings.title: No unit test for _utc_iso_now() helper
findings.description: Helper function _utc_iso_now() at L1308 lacks direct unit test coverage. This function is critical for run-id generation and timestamp consistency across the run lifecycle.
findings.evidence: Searched test files in tests/cli/eval/ - no direct test found for _utc_iso_now(). Function is used in eval_run at L1707 for started_iso timestamp.
findings.recommendation: Add unit test: test_utc_iso_now_returns_z_suffix_iso_format() to verify the YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ format and that the +00:00 is replaced with Z.
cross_references: tests/cli/eval/test_artifact_layout.py:80-92 tests compose_run_id with ISO strings but doesn't test the clock helper directly

findings.title: _new_run_id() wrapper lacks edge case testing
findings.description: While _new_run_id is tested indirectly via integration tests, there's no direct unit test for edge cases like microsecond collision (same started_at called twice rapidly).
findings.evidence: test_single_command.py references _new_run_id at L1328 for symbol contract but doesn't test collision behavior. The underlying compose_run_id is deterministic (same inputs → same output) but rapid sequential calls with identical started_at aren't tested.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_new_run_id_collision_same_microsecond() to verify that two calls with identical started_at and suite_name produce the same run_id (determinism), and that this is the intended behavior (not a bug).

findings.title: No unit test for _default_output_dir() helper
findings.description: _default_output_dir() at L1335 lacks direct unit test. Function constructs the default per-run output directory but isn't tested for path construction correctness independent of integration tests.
findings.evidence: Function delegates to compose_run_dir but no test verifies the wrapper's signature or that it correctly passes started_at and suite_name through.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_default_output_dir_matches_compose_run_dir() to verify the function returns the same path as compose_run_dir(Path.cwd(), started_at, suite_name).

findings.title: No unit test for _can_install_signal_handler() helper
findings.description: _can_install_signal_handler() at L1346 lacks direct unit test. Function checks if current thread is main thread but has no test coverage for non-main-thread case.
findings.evidence: Function uses threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread() check but no test verifies the False branch (non-main thread scenario).
findings.recommendation: Add tests: test_can_install_signal_handler_true_on_main_thread() and test_can_install_signal_handler_false_on_worker_thread() spawning a Thread to verify both branches.

findings.title: No test for _resolve_executor_factory() unknown factory name handling
findings.description: _resolve_executor_factory() at L1390 currently returns _NullLifecycleExecutor but there's no test for what happens when the production executor is wired and an unknown factory name is requested.
findings.evidence: Function is monkeypatched in tests (test_exit_codes.py:391) but no test verifies error handling for invalid factory resolution. Current implementation is stub-only (M5/M6 blocker).
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_resolve_executor_factory_unknown_name_raises() for when production wiring lands, to verify ValueError or similar is raised for unknown factory names.
cross_references: tests/cli/eval/test_exit_codes.py:391-399 checks _NullLifecycleExecutor type but doesn't test factory resolution errors

findings.title: _run_one_spec() lacks direct unit test coverage
findings.description: _run_one_spec() at L1405 is a critical per-spec worker function but only tested via integration tests. No unit test for timeout_mult edge cases or executor_factory injection.
findings.evidence: Function is referenced in test_no_pty_exclusion.py:298, test_no_mcp_skip.py:472, and test_exit_codes.py:36 but all are integration-level. No unit test for spec.timeout_sec=None vs >0, or timeout_mult=0.5 vs 2.0 scaling.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests: test_run_one_spec_applies_timeout_mult() to verify timeout_mult correctly scales spec.timeout_sec, and test_run_one_spec_ignores_mult_when_spec_timeout_none().

findings.title: _compute_run_stats() lacks edge case tests
findings.description: _compute_run_stats() at L1477 has no unit tests for empty outcomes list, all-passed, all-failed, or manifest_n mismatch scenarios.
findings.evidence: Function is used in integration tests but no dedicated unit test. Edge cases: outcomes=[], all PASS, all FAIL, manifest_n != len(outcomes) aren't explicitly tested.

findings.title: _format_run_summary_line() lacks Unicode edge case test
findings.description: _format_run_summary_line() at L1526 formats run summary for stdout but has no test for Unicode characters in suite_name or run_id.
findings.evidence: Function formats a string including summary.run_id which could contain suite_name with Unicode. No test verifies UTF-8 handling or terminal-safe rendering.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_format_run_summary_line_handles_unicode_suite_name() with suite_name containing emoji or non-ASCII chars.

findings.title: Exit code constants lack library-level value pin tests
findings.description: RUN_CLEAN_EXIT_CODE, RUN_FAILURES_EXIT_CODE, RUN_INTERRUPTED_EXIT_CODE constants at L570-580 are tested at process boundary (test_exit_codes.py) but lack library-level constant value assertions.
findings.evidence: test_exit_codes.py:405-408 asserts EXIT_INTERRUPTED == 3 at library boundary. Similar assertions for RUN_CLEAN_EXIT_CODE=0 and RUN_FAILURES_EXIT_CODE=1 are missing.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_run_exit_code_constants_match_design_spec() to assert RUN_CLEAN_EXIT_CODE==0, RUN_FAILURES_EXIT_CODE==1, RUN_INTERRUPTED_EXIT_CODE==3 at library level (not just process boundary).

findings.title: Allowlist tautology regression test missing
findings.description: Commit dce3c3cb added scratch-root allowlist closure fixing a tautology bug, but there's no regression test pinning that the output_dir parameter to resolve_scratch_root cannot be the same as the candidate path being validated.
findings.evidence: config.py:202-213 documents the tautology risk: 'Do NOT pass the raw operator-supplied --output-dir here at the first gate. Doing so makes the candidate path equal to an allowlist entry by construction.' No test explicitly exercises this forbidden pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_scratch_root_allowlist_rejects_tautology() that attempts resolve_scratch_root('/etc/passwd', output_dir='/etc/passwd') and verifies it FAILS (not passes). This pins the dce3c3cb fix.
cross_references: tests/cli/eval/test_scratch_root_allowlist.py:79-87 tests output_dir is call-scoped but not the tautology case

findings.title: Missing test for relative path resolving outside scratch_root
findings.description: containment_guard documentation mentions 'relative path that resolves outside (e.g., subdir/../../../etc/passwd)' but no test explicitly exercises this case.
findings.evidence: test_path_traversal.py tests ../home, /etc, and bare .., but not multi-level traversal like eval_id='subdir/../../../etc/passwd'. containment_guard check 3 (L320-330) uses Path.resolve(strict=True) which should catch this, but it's not explicitly tested.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_containment_guard_rejects_multi_level_dotdot_traversal() creating home_path with multiple ../ segments that escape scratch_root after resolution.

findings.title: Missing test for symlink pointing outside scratch_root from within home_path
findings.description: containment_guard check 3 catches 'symlinked component inside home_path points outside scratch_root' but test coverage focuses on symlink AT the home_path level, not INSIDE it.
findings.evidence: test_symlink_attacks.py:261-273 tests scratch_root as symlink and home_path as symlink, but not a symlink INSIDE home_path (e.g., home_path/artifacts -> /tmp/evil). Check 3 at L324 uses resolve(strict=True) which should catch this.
findings.recommendation: Add test: test_containment_guard_rejects_symlink_inside_home_path() creating home_path/subdir as symlink to /tmp/outside, then verifying containment_guard raises home_path_escape.
cross_references: tests/cli/eval/test_symlink_attacks.py focuses on scratch_root and home_path as symlinks, not contents

cross_cutting_observations.title: Helper-level unit tests vs integration-only coverage
cross_cutting_observations.observation: The 11 helpers added in commit e6368db8 are tested primarily through integration tests (eval_run end-to-end). While this provides high confidence in the happy path, it leaves edge cases and error branches untested. Unit tests would allow faster iteration and clearer failure diagnosis.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Integration-only coverage means edge case failures (e.g., _compute_run_stats with empty outcomes, _format_run_summary_line with Unicode) won't surface until full eval_run execution, increasing debug time.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Allowlist tautology regression risk
cross_cutting_observations.observation: The dce3c3cb fix for the allowlist tautology is documented in config.py:202-213 but not enforced by a test. A future refactor could accidentally reintroduce the bug (passing candidate as output_dir parameter) without detection.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: High - this is a security boundary. Without a regression test, the tautology could silently return, allowing writes to /etc, /root, etc.
cross_cutting_observations.recommended_action: Add test_scratch_root_allowlist_rejects_tautology() as highest priority security test.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Mocks of security boundaries are red flags
cross_cutting_observations.observation: No tests mock isolation.py or containment_guard (good!). All containment tests use real filesystem operations and actual path resolution. This is the correct approach for security-critical code.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Positive - the security boundary is integration-tested, not mocked. Continue this pattern.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Click CliRunner() API migration (mix_stderr removal)
cross_cutting_observations.observation: Commit 08183738 removed Click mix_stderr= calls. Tests in test_eval_run.py, test_describe.py, test_list.py use CliRunner() with zero args (correct for Click 8.3.2+). No test verifies stderr/stdout are correctly separated under the new API.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Low - existing tests pass, but explicit stderr assertion coverage could be stronger (e.g., test_eval_run_outputs_error_to_stderr_only).
cross_cutting_observations.recommended_action: Add test verifying that error messages go to result.stderr, not result.stdout, post-Click-8.3.2.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Coverage gate tests are comprehensive
cross_cutting_observations.observation: Coverage gate (coverage.py) has excellent test coverage: pass case (test_coverage_gate.py:191-196), fail case (199-228), missing coverage data (150-158), malformed data (160-165). FR-G5 AC is fully pinned.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Positive - this is a model for other modules.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Reporter ban-import rule is enforced via ruff TID251
cross_cutting_observations.observation: test_ban_import_rule.py (L108-129) verifies ruff catches 'import anthropic' with TID251. This is a static check (good!), not a runtime import test. No test verifies reporter.py itself doesn't import anthropic at runtime.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Medium - static check is strong, but a runtime assertion (import reporter; assert 'anthropic' not in sys.modules) would be defense-in-depth.
cross_cutting_observations.recommended_action: Add test_reporter_does_not_import_anthropic_at_runtime() importing reporter module and asserting anthropic isn't in sys.modules.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Artifact layout tests cover all suite/run/spec combinations
cross_cutting_observations.observation: test_artifact_layout.py (L180-214) tests allocate_per_eval_paths for create=True and create=False, idempotency, and path structure. Tests cover compose_run_id determinism (L54-77), compose_run_dir shape (L120-152), and parse_run_dir_components round-trip (L230-255). All FR-G4 AC are pinned.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Positive - comprehensive coverage of path-shape functions.

cross_cutting_observations.title: SIGINT during run exit code 130 test is forward-blocked
cross_cutting_observations.observation: test_exit_codes.py:363-450 tests SIGINT → exit 3 but is skipped until M5/M6 production executor lands (L391-399). Current _NullLifecycleExecutor returns instantly so SIGINT never hits mid-run. Test is well-structured to auto-unskip when blocker clears.
cross_cutting_observations.impact: Low - test exists and will activate when executor lands. No action needed beyond monitoring M5/M6.

critical_gaps: Allowlist tautology regression test (dce3c3cb fix not pinned by test)
No unit tests for 8 of 11 helpers added in e6368db8
No test for multi-level ../ path traversal in containment_guard
strengths: Coverage gate tests are comprehensive (pass, fail, missing data, malformed data all covered)
Artifact layout tests cover all FR-G4 acceptance criteria
Security boundaries (containment_guard, resolve_scratch_root) are integration-tested, not mocked
Exit code constants are tested at process boundary (subprocess.run) not just library level
